# How should end-effector disturbances be generated during force-tracking operation training?

> **Current answer:** In the G1/T1 settings of FALCON, the end-effector Jacobian, gravity torque, and joint torque are constrained in three-dimensional disturbances, and their scale is gradually expanded in conjunction with a shared proprioceptive upper and lower-body strategy. This approach yields lower force-tracking errors compared to force-torque perception, upper-body PD/IK, and same-stack single-body RL in real-world scenarios. The static approximation does not equal actual machine contact or thermal safety guarantees.

## Assumptions

- End-effector Jacobians and joint torque limits are available in simulation.
- Lower-body locomotion and upper-body joint tracking form separable objectives with shared proprioception.

## Diagnosis and verification

- First verify the applicable robot, simulator, controller, environment, and assumptions, then follow the evidence locators below to inspect the original experiment or implementation.

## Result

- In the G1/T1 settings of FALCON, the end-effector Jacobian, gravity torque, and joint torque are constrained in three-dimensional disturbances, and their scale is gradually expanded in conjunction with a shared proprioceptive upper and lower-body strategy. This approach yields lower force-tracking errors compared to force-torque perception, upper-body PD/IK, and same-stack single-body RL in real-world scenarios. The static approximation does not equal actual machine contact or thermal safety guarantees.

## Limitations

- End-effector Jacobians and joint torque limits are available in simulation.
- Lower-body locomotion and upper-body joint tracking form separable objectives with shared proprioception.

## Safety notes

- **Validated in simulation:** Yes
- **Command limits:** Before hardware use, derive robot- and firmware-specific position, velocity, torque and contact-force limits; paper training clips are not deployment limits.
- **Emergency stop:** Before force interaction, test an independent human-accessible emergency stop and verify stopping at the selected low-energy envelope.
- **Protective controls:** Use a cleared exclusion zone, secured load, compatible fall protection, thermal/current monitoring, and a human safety operator.
- **Robot-specific warning:** Evidence covers only the reported Unitree G1 and Booster T1 configurations; actuator, wrist, hand and SDK differences require a new review.
- **Staged deployment:** Proceed from fixed-seed simulation to cross-simulator replay, supported no-contact motion, low-force single-axis contact, then bounded multi-axis tasks with logged abort criteria.
